title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) that evaluated whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a deterministic synthetic intent→configuration task bank and a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, representative validator-trace excerpts, quantitative analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, and artifact-grounded prescriptions (fault-injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value in follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction:
Automated NetOps workflows increasingly use generative models to translate operator intent into actionable configuration sequences. Operational safety requires mechanisms that prevent syntactic, semantic, or policy-violating outputs from being accepted or executed. A common operational architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a generator (LLM) proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator checks mechanistic constraints and policy rules, and repair logic attempts remediation or escalates for human review. Prior work demonstrates GVR-style architectures in code and system settings and motivates their use in NetOps, but systematic, preregistered, artifact-archived measurements of validator coverage (false-positive and false-negative rates), detection latency, and their predictive utility for end-to-end guarded success are lacking [1].

We preregistered study AC-2026-03 to measure whether a multidimensional validator metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, detection latency, operational-impact proxy) explains more variance in end-to-end task success than a single verifier pass rate. The design uses a paired, shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task the generator produced one initial candidate that was reused verbatim by both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator + repair permitted). Under these semantics any paired difference can arise only from downstream validator-triggered repair, not from independent generator sampling. Our contribution is a fully preregistered, artifact-archived execution and an exact report of the degenerate confirmatory outcome (complete ceiling) together with data-driven recommendations for follow-up preregistered arms that can render validator metrics estimable.
sections.related_work:
GVR and closed-loop verifier layers have been proposed to mitigate stochastic generator defects and to provide deterministic acceptance criteria in code and system domains [1]. Recent NetOps and AIOps benchmark efforts highlight agent fragility under ticket noise, false premises, and plausible-sounding but incorrect outputs, motivating insertion of verifier layers and auditable decision traces [2],[3]. System reports and prototypes describe self-healing orchestrators and verifier-guided repair that reduce silent failures in controlled evaluations [4]. Broader surveys of LLMs in telecommunications and NetOps discuss adaptation and verification trade-offs and call for metricized analyses that account for verification cost as well as nominal correctness [5].

These records justify studying validator measurement but do not themselves provide a standardized, empirically estimable validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows. We therefore designed a preregistered, reproducible experiment to begin filling that measurement gap while explicitly treating prior demonstrations as architectural motivation rather than proof of broad validator coverage.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered elements (machine-readable plan archived): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Power planning targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power under conservative assumptions; bootstrap stability checks were preregistered.

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty labels 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task payload contains an initial_state, an expected_final_state, an explicit intent description, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. These structured constraints make each task amenable to mechanistic validation by a deterministic validator. Task selection followed the preregistered deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1). Contamination rules (SHA-256 duplicate exclusion and embedding-cosine > 0.95 semantic-similarity exclusion) were preregistered; no exclusions occurred in the run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model, sampling, and adapter semantics. The declared model was gpt-5-mini as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The execution manifest reports model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Important configuration note grounded in the execution artifact: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). Null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling variability may still occur. The adapter's provider-call audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200.

Validator and scoring rule. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements syntactic and mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields including normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair traces when applied. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call per episode; repairs would be recorded (repair_provider_trace_path, repair_applied toggled). The execution artifacts show repair_applied = false for all episodes.

Execution policy, missingness, and exclusions. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). The missingness plan specified complete-pair analysis with sensitivity checks that treat missing guarded episodes as failures in sensitivity analyses. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200. No preregistered exclusion rules were triggered. All raw responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No contamination exclusions occurred.

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. All reported numeric artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and match the values above.

Representative validator-trace excerpt (artifact-grounded). A compact exemplar from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (verbatim fields from the artifact) illustrates validator semantics and why no repair occurred: pair_id = pair-000004; normalized_configuration = "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"; parsed_command_count = 4; required_command_count = 4; observed_touched_field_count = 3; valid = true; repair_applied = false; validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; validator_version = 5.0. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode.

Secondary and exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN estimates are degenerate (no observed false positives or false negatives) because all initial candidates passed mechanistic checks. Detection-latency and repair-invocation distributions are uninformative (repair_applied = false for all episodes). The execution bundle nevertheless contains full per-episode traces (execution/raw_results.jsonl) that support reanalysis under alternative scoring rules or under injected-fault conditions described below.

Interpretation of ceiling outcome. Shared_initial_candidate semantics ensured baseline and guarded evaluated the identical generated candidate per pair; hence any paired difference could only result from validator-triggered repair. The degenerate all-valid outcome arises from three linked, artifact-grounded determinants visible in the archive: (1) the deterministic task generator produced reference answers and generator seeds such that the sampled candidates satisfied the validator's mechanistic constraints across the selected index set; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime removed generator variability as a source of disagreement; and (3) the validator checks mechanistic syntactic and policy constraints but necessarily lacks an independent external intent model and therefore cannot detect some classes of correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent mismatches. These factors jointly explain absence of repairs and the zero-variance primary estimand.
sections.discussion:
Inferential limits and lessons. The preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics isolates downstream repair effects but concentrates the risk of a single-sample ceiling when generator and validator align. With observed baseline success = 1.0 the paired estimator has zero variance: both McNemar and bootstrap procedures are degenerate and cannot detect the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement. This is an artifact-grounded inferential null: it indicates that under the present synthetic bank and sampling regime there were no mechanically detectable defects for the validator to catch.

What the result does and does not show. The outcome does not imply validators are universally unnecessary; rather, it indicates that for this synthetic bank, the specific generator seeds and the validator's mechanistic specification produced no detectable structural or policy violations. The result also illustrates an important methodological point for preregistered GVR measurement: shared_initial_candidate semantics rigorously attributes any improvement to downstream repair but also reduces the opportunity for generator variability to create failures that the validator could intercept. Future preregistered designs must explicitly balance isolation of repair effects with controlled baseline failure prevalence.

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments. The archived execution artifacts support concrete, reproducible next-step arms that will render validator metrics estimable:
  1) Fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically inject controlled faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). This produces measurable baseline invalidity and makes repair utility observable. The execution bundle already supports deterministic task replacement and contamination checks to implement this without manual intervention.
  2) Multi-sample stochastic generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task and allow the guarded pipeline to accept any validator-approved draw or to request repair. Multiple independent samples per task expose generator variability and increase opportunities for the validator to reject some draws and trigger repair.
  3) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one other model family. Contrasting validators quantifies sensitivity to validator design and improves external validity beyond the single validator used here.
Each prescribed arm is implementable using the adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 semantics recorded in the execution bundle and will yield non-degenerate data to estimate FP/FN, detection latency, repair impact, and predictive R^2 against an operational-impact proxy as originally planned.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate intentionally isolates repair but introduced single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: validator.valid encodes mechanistic correctness but may miss semantic intent misalignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model (gpt-5-mini), and single deterministic validator limit generalization to production networks and alternative model families. Conclusion validity: absence of variance in the primary outcome prevents inferential conclusions about validator benefit from this execution alone. All these limitations and the precise artifact provenance are documented in the execution and analysis bundles.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed mechanistic checks; no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. This artifact-grounded result is reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and present concrete, preregistered follow-up prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. These follow-up arms are directly supported by the archived adapter semantics and task-generation infrastructure and therefore amenable to future confirmatory preregistered runs that will measure validator coverage and repair utility empirically.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
